AUTHOR: Jia
TITLE: Underwater Object Detection in Marine Ranching Based on Improved YOLOv8
VENUE: JOURNAL OF MARINE SCIENCE AND ENGINEERING
REGION: Luhaifeng and Laizhou Bay marine ranches, Shandong, China (+ NOAA US west coast; URPC China)
SPECIES: fish (single class) plus echinus, holothurian, scallop, starfish
DATA: Pooled: URPC2021 + Wild Fish Marker/Labeled Fishes in the Wild (NOAA) + own marine-ranch seafloor observation videos/images (2021)
D_EV: Sec. 3.2: 'all data were randomly divided at a ratio of 8:1:1 among the training set, validation set, and test set'
R_EV: Sec. 3.2/3.4: single pooled dataset randomly split; Table 2 reports AP on that test set only
C_EV: no statement found (only 'mAP is for an IoU threshold of 0.5'; no confidence threshold reported)
E_EV: Sec. 3.4: 'The main evaluation indicators used in this study were the precision, recall, AP, and mAP'
ARCH: Improved YOLOv8n (InceptionNeXt backbone block, SEAM attention, CIoU+NWD loss); baselines Faster R-CNN, YOLOv5n, YOLOv7-tiny, YOLOv8n
METR: Precision, Recall, AP per class, mAP@0.5, FPS, FLOPs, Params
NOTE: Multi-taxon; fish AP reported separately (Improved YOLOv8 fish AP 89.5%). Test set mixes benchmark (URPC, LFW) and own marine-ranch field images; proportions not reported. Sec. 3.5 counts of detected fish in sample images are model-vs-model comparisons, not human counts. Visibility only discussed generically in Introduction/Conclusion.
